title: cairn-checks-the-floor-before-it-resolves
owner: codemother owns the care of this seam (ruling 2026-09-06); CC/Opus builds. The venv lay-down and the db start each keep their one existing address; bin/cairn calls them.
intention: The `cairn` command checks the floor before it resolves anything: the venv exists, the db is reachable, the instance is set up — and lays what is missing rather than failing into a device that cannot run.
why: Akien's launch chain, told for the second time 2026-09-06 and recorded verbatim at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md. Cast the same day so the intention carries a ticket (CLAUDE.md: an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect).
traces_to: Law 1 (the floor is settled once, by the command, not re-derived by every device) and Law 7 (a missing floor is loud at the one surface the operator is looking at). Akien 2026-09-06 verbatim: 'the cairn command sees that the venv exists, and the db, and that it's all set up' — and 'everything automatically lazy inits'.

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — bin/proofs/test_cairn_floor.py (new, beside bin/cairn): isolated HOME, three fault injections each answered in one invocation, happy-path timing recorded. Feeds back naming the check that failed. Durability: committed in cairn; tester seal.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when: (1) with the venv renamed away, `cairn librarian show status` lays a venv and then answers, in one invocation; (2) with the db stopped, the same command starts it and answers; (3) on the happy path the preflight adds under 10ms to bin/cairn's time-to-exec (measure n=15 interleaved, the launchers charter's method); (4) `grep -n venv bin/cairn` is no longer empty (it is empty today, measured 2026-09-06). WRONG INTENT if the preflight grows a second copy of the venv lay-down or the db start — those live in one place each and the command calls them.

questions.a: Two named. (1) 'The db' is the local Postgres on 5432 and starting it is within the user's reach via sudo-relay — standing on this host; phrased as reachability with 'start' as the local remedy so a second host of the instance is not foreclosed. (2) The superclaude launcher's venv preflight can be lifted into a shared function rather than copied — standing; it is a shell block today and becomes bin/cairn's, with the launcher calling it. Neither is load-bearing beyond the build.

One point was asserted wrapped and was not: what 'it's all set up' means concretely. Now wrapped as: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/ exists with flags/ and the instance homes the resolver symlinks into (~/.cairn/devices/<device>/0/bin/). The preflight lays that shape from class-space when missing, using the existing instance setup path, and refuses (loud, nonzero, named) if it cannot.

Consulted the lab. launchers charter's preflight has the same why (floor before anything runs); this widens its reach to the command every caller shares — a distinction to record, and the launcher keeps its own until the command's is proven. Ruling 2026-08-11 (no system-level startup) is honoured: everything here is a lazy lay-down at command time. No Law collides; Law 7 is served.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) the three checks in order and their remedies — venv: `~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3` exists else call the launcher's lay-down; db: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432` (or db_domain's probe if one exists — check cairn/devices/db_domain first) else the store's start path; instance: `~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/` exists else the instance setup; (b) that bin/cairn is bash and must exec the device launcher at the end unchanged; (c) the measurement harness — copy the launchers charter's interleaved n=15 method, report median with min/max, and keep the number in the charter without a gate; (d) don't — no python startup on the happy path (that alone is ~30ms), no daemon, no cache file that could go stale. All written into the ticket's how.

constraints: No change to the ground loop's contents: pulse, control flags, devices-found list — ever (Akien 2026-09-06).
One pipe: device → IPC → own shim → bus → addressee's shim → IPC → addressee; the db alone is exempt (volume).
how: bin/cairn gains a preflight before the device resolver: (1) ~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3 exists, else run the existing venv lay-down (the superclaude launcher already has a preflight that lays the venv — lift that, don't copy it); (2) the db answers on 5432 via db_domain's own probe, else start it the way the store's own tooling does; (3) ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/ exists with the instance shape, else run the instance setup. Each check is a cheap read on the happy path (measured budget: the whole cairn command must stay under the launcher's 76ms median to exec). A failed lay-down is loud and exits nonzero with the check named; it never falls through into the resolver.
links: launchers charter (cairn/launchers/) — the venv preflight to lift, and the measurement method
watchme: none, because the floor is checked on every command by construction; the only operational signal is the happy-path cost, which the proof records and the launchers charter's what_a_launch_COSTS entry (cairn/launchers/intention+why.json) is the precedent for keeping without a gate

intent.what: The `cairn` command checks the floor before it resolves anything: the venv exists, the db is reachable, the instance is set up — and lays what is missing rather than failing into a device that cannot run.

challenge.better_approach: Leaving the floor to the superclaude launcher (which already lays the venv for a CC session) was the status quo; it means `cairn` typed in a bare shell, or by aider, or by codemother, gets no floor. The command is the one entry every caller shares, so the check belongs there. A separate `cairn setup` verb was the other candidate; it survives as the thing the preflight CALLS, not as a step the operator must remember (Law 1).
challenge.prior_art: launchers/superclaude preflight (venv floor, measured to exec) — lift it. db_domain's connect probe and the store's start path. The instance shape under ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<n>/ is already the addressing rule in CLAUDE.md. Nothing in the field to graft; this is a preflight.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That 'the db' means the local Postgres on 5432 and that starting it is something the user manager may do without sudo — true on this host today via sudo-relay; on a second host of the same instance the db is the master elsewhere and 'reachable' replaces 'started'. The check must be phrased as reachability, with 'start' as the local remedy.
challenge.real_collision: None found. The launchers charter's preflight has the same why (the floor is laid before anything runs); this generalizes its reach from one launcher to the command every launcher shares. Distinction to record: the launcher keeps its own preflight until the command's is proven, then calls the command's.

why_beneath_the_why: Akien 2026-09-06: 'if everything goes thru one pipe, we learn faster' and 'everythign automatically lazy inits' — the operator types one command and the system stands itself up behind it, on one pipe, with nothing to remember.
